column1: # vdi-r2.tsv -- VDI reference dumper, round 2: full opcode sweep.
# Round 1 (vdi-r1.tsv, CRC FFF2281E) stays frozen with the dumps already
# measured on EmuTOS 1.4 and TOS 3.06. This is a SEPARATE table: a case id is
# a physical line number and the file CRC binds every dump to it, so a growing
# table would invalidate measurements already taken.
# Goal: cover every VDI opcode that can be measured, so the dumps are a basis
# for generated Rust tests against tos-api/src/vdi/.
# Every opcode and every input arity below was derived mechanically from the
# EmuTOS handlers -- the jump tables in vdi/vdi_main.c:32-111 for the opcode
# map and output counts, and each handler's own INTIN[n]/PTSIN[n] reads for
# the inputs. Nothing here is written from memory. The GDP sub-op inputs come
# from vdi/vdi_gdp.c (gdp_curve reads PTSIN[0..3] plus PTSIN[4] for the circle
# and PTSIN[6] otherwise, and INTIN[0..1] as begin/end angle; gdp_rbox reads
# PTSIN[0..1]); the escape sub-ops from docs/api/vdi/_escape.md.
# Excluded, with the reason, per cases/COVERAGE.md: opcodes 1, 2, 100 and 101
# (would destroy the workstation the run measures through); 124 and 128 (read
# live mouse and keyboard, so they would differ between two runs on one
# machine); 14, 112, 118, 119, 120, 125-127 and 134 (leave state the reset
# cannot undo); 28 and 31 (request-mode input, blocks on the operator);
# 109, 110 and 121 (need MFDB pointers in contrl[7..10], which differ per
# machine and have no comparison rule yet); escape sub-ops 2, 3 and 17
# (switch screen mode, or trigger a real printer dump).
# Appending only: a new case goes at the end.
# opcode
# --- no-ops: an unimplemented opcode is observable behaviour too -------
